body:
Hello! I think the main problem here is using `compiler.compileModuleAsync`

According to the [docs](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/docs/PUBLIC_API.md#supported-public-api-surface-of-angular)

> One intentional omission from this list is @angular/compiler, which is currently considered a low level api and is subject to internal changes. 

So don't use it. 

To test memory leak i would advice you enable prod mode. 

Each time you call `compiler.compileModuleAsync` you add new key to `_tokenKeyCache` Map that is used internally.
@trotyl Yeah, you're right. And it throws error `Runtime compiler is not loaded` if we don't provide `JitCompiler` from `@angular/compiler`
@alexzuza `JitCompiler` is provided by `@angular/platform-browser-dynamic`, user won't touch any symbol defined in `@angular/compiler`, everything is still under public API.

Thanks for pointing this out. It lies in `@angular/platform-browser-dynamic` only starting from 5.x.x https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/18683/commits/40754da9f9054a602f9e1b323f16482aa5b1119f
It also tells us that we should not rely on it until it becames stable

That's not the point, the API usage is only defined by declaration. And what declared here is `Compiler` in `@angular/core`, not `JitCompiler` in `@angular/compiler`, which makes it a public API, it does not matter where the implementation is.

And `Compiler` exists start from [`2.0.0-rc.4`](https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/bf598d6b8b978dfca2dfe8d3cfb38f39b4653138#diff-b63a2f91aa674bf94a5d02aee347d16d) with the mark `@stable`, it's even within deprecation strategy.

No one is relying on `JitCompiler`, only `Compiler` should be used. Since the term `provide` is ambiguous in Angular, just change to "`Compiler` is given by `@angular/platform-browser-dynamic`" could make it clear.
Any idea when will this be fixed? I'm stuck releasing due to this nasty bug.

issue.title: Performance issue when instantiating multiple instances

repository.name: ngx-color-picker
repository.description: Color picker widget for the Angular (version 2 and newer)

issue.body: Hello, I'm using this directive on a dynamic component which I create and then destroy multiple times, depending on what items I click in the DOM. I've notices a high load since I switched to this color picker and a lot of bottlenecks after a 10-20 instantiation. I've tried replicating this without the colorpicker, but it worked smooth (no bottlenecks). Is there any way I can bypass this issue? Thanks!

body:
My team was just bitten by this bug (or a similar one) in a new context: our Jasmine test suite. We are on Angular 1 and 5 in a hybrid app, and are still using `UpgradeAdapter`. Something during the bootstrapping process calls `PlatformRef.bootstrapModule`, which 16 calls up the stack gets to `tokenKey()` passing it e.g. an array of `ComponentFactory`s. This happens at the start of every test, so all those old `ComponentFactories` and many other things are kept in memory for the duration of the test suite.

Our suite no longer works because it runs the browser out of memory. We will work around it by splitting our suite into multiple smaller suites to run separately for now.

Please let me know if this belongs in a separate ticket, or if more specifics would be helpful. Thanks!

I noticed that `TestBed.configureTestModule` created a `DynamicTestModule` under the cover. And each instance of DynamicTestModule will be reference by the `_tokenKeyCache`.

And from https://angular.io/guide/testing#component-test-basics, each test case will call `TestBed.configureTestModule`. So each test case will be leaking an instance of `DynamicTestModule`.

Internally each `DynamicTestModule` instances a compiled list of providers. And if you use `ValueProvider`, it will have a reference to an objects instead of a class.

So for a sizable test suites, this could add up.
